Working notes — east-region ticket routing

- Tickets REQ-2400–2409: large east-region requests (shipment, claim, invoice, refund) need assignment to the right desk.
- Tried option C (“regional office” / “region”) on all 10. Every outcome: Rejected, +0.00. Conclusion: C is invalid for this request class. Do not choose C again.
- Sender/team, subject wording, and urgency cues (“no rush”, “client asking twice”, “second attempt”, “before end of day”, “confirm receipt”) did not make C valid. They are not reliable routing criteria.
- Remaining plausible options: A (standard queue), B (priority desk), and possibly D if shown. Next, test A or B.
- Leading hypothesis: B (priority desk), because requests are described as “large” and all originate from the east region. No positive evidence yet.
- If B is rejected, test A. Keep tracking outcomes to confirm the correct desk and whether request type changes routing.
- Avoid repeating failed C attempts; seek a successful outcome before generalizing further.

Working notes — east-region ticket routing

- Tickets REQ-2400–2419: large east-region requests (shipment, claim, invoice, refund) need routing.
- Option C (“regional office”/“region”): rejected on all tested requests, +0.00. Invalid; do not choose C.
- Option B (priority desk): tested on REQ-2410–2419. Accepted (+1.00) for invoice and shipment. Rejected (+0.00) for all refunds: 2411, 2413, 2414, 2418.
- Routing depends on request type, not sender/team, subject wording, urgency cues, or “regional office” phrases. Examples: “no rush”, “second attempt”, “confirm receipt”, scanned vs typed, Field Sales/Regional Ops/Finance did not determine outcome.
- Current rule: large east-region invoice -> B. Large east-region shipment -> B.
- Current hypothesis: large east-region refund -> A (standard queue). B and C failed for refunds; A is the remaining likely option. Test A on next refund.
- If A fails for refund, test D if shown. Keep tracking refund outcomes and any claim cases; do not assume claims follow invoice/shipment or refund without evidence.
- Avoid repeating failed C. Avoid B for refunds unless new evidence contradicts.

Working notes — east-region ticket routing

- Tickets REQ-2400–2429: large east-region requests (invoice, shipment, refund, claim) need routing.
- Option C (“regional office”/“region”): rejected when tested; invalid. Do not choose C.
- Invoice: B (priority desk) accepted on REQ-2410–2419, 2420, 2423–2426. Rule: large east-region invoice -> B.
- Shipment: B accepted on REQ-2410–2419, 2427–2428. Rule: large east-region shipment -> B.
- Refund: B rejected (2411, 2413, 2414, 2418). A rejected on 2421 and 2429. C invalid. So refund is not A, B, or C. D untested for refund; test D on next refund if available.
- Claim: only tested option D on 2422, rejected. A/B/C untested for claims. Do not infer claim rule from invoice/shipment/refund.
- Routing depends on request type, not sender/team, subject wording, urgency cues, or “regional office” phrases. New examples reinforce this: Regional Ops, Partner Accounts, Field Sales, Finance Desk; “same as last month,” “no rush,” “confirm receipt,” “client asking twice,” “before end of day,” “second attempt,” “first form bounced” did not change invoice/shipment/refund outcomes.
- Next tests: refund -> D. Claim -> test A/B/C as available; D already failed for claim.
- Avoid repeating failed C. Avoid A/B for refunds unless contradicted by new evidence.

- Routing depends on request type, not sender/team, subject wording, urgency cues, or “regional office” phrases. New examples reinforce: Field Sales, Regional Ops, Partner Accounts, Client Services; “same as last month,” “no rush,” “confirm receipt,” “client asking twice,” “before end of day,” “regional office,” “scanned not typed” did not change invoice/shipment outcomes; claim accepted despite regional office phrase.

Working notes — east-region ticket routing
- Large east-region tickets: REQ-2400+.
- C (“regional office”/“region”) invalid for all observed types. Do not choose C.
- Routing depends on request type, not sender/team, wording, urgency, or “regional office.” New examples reinforce this: invoice accepted with varied senders/subjects; shipment/refund rejected despite varied wording.
- Invoice: large east-region -> B. Confirmed through REQ-2448 (new: 2441, 2444, 2445, 2448). Keep B.
- Claim: large east-region -> A. REQ-2430 accepted; D rejected on 2422. B/C untested; A works.
- Shipment: previously B, but now contradicted. B rejected on REQ-2443, 2446, 2447. Do not use B for shipment. C invalid. A untested—try A if shipment appears, or escalate if unsure.
- Refund: unresolved/all options invalid. A rejected 2421, 2429, 2440; B rejected 2411, 2413, 2414, 2418, 2442, 2449; C invalid; D rejected 2434, 2438, 2439. Do not repeat A/B/C/D; flag/escalate new refunds unless new option/evidence.

Working notes — east-region ticket routing
- Large east-region tickets: REQ-2400+.
- Routing depends on request type; sender/team, wording, urgency, and “regional office” phrases are not decisive. New examples reinforce this.
- Invoice: large east-region -> B. Confirmed REQ-2441, 2444, 2445, 2448, 2455. Keep B.
- Shipment: large east-region -> A. Confirmed REQ-2451–2454, 2458. B rejected REQ-2443, 2446, 2447. Use A, not B.
- Refund: large east-region -> C. REQ-2457 accepted C. Earlier A/B/D rejected (A: 2421, 2429, 2440; B: 2411, 2413, 2414, 2418, 2442, 2449; D: 2434, 2438, 2439). Correct old “C invalid” note: C is valid for refund. Use C.
- Claim: contradictory. A accepted once (2430) but rejected REQ-2450, 2456, 2459. D rejected 2422. B untested. C uncertain (not universally invalid). Do not use A for claim. If claim appears, try B only if forced; otherwise escalate/flag.
- C: not universally invalid; valid for refund. For invoice/shipment use B/A respectively. For claim, C uncertain.
- Current rules: invoice -> B; shipment -> A; refund -> C; claim -> avoid A (B/untested; escalate if unsure). Avoid repeating rejected options.
